$comment: AgentCake's environment layer: each rule reads one trace of automation, of a named agent product, of a cloud machine or of an extension acting on the page. agentcake/detect/env_rules.py evaluates `match` (grammar in its docstring) against the signals env_signals.py builds, and a session-scope rule also against `touch` (whether the browser says it is a phone or tablet); a hit carries id, layer, kind, half, strength, grade and the value that matched. `scope`: page = on each page view, landing = the first page view only, session = the session as a whole. `botscent`: the botscent page-half reasons a rule stands for, so the two can be compared on recorded sessions. `names`: the agent product or automation tool a rule names; `suggests`: a name a rule hints at without proving it. `enabled`: the default; the user's config can switch any rule. `setting`: on a rule that is off by default, the page-script setting that turns it on: the rule runs on a visit recorded with that setting on, as the visit's page records say (signals.script_settings names the page record fields that say how the site owner had set cake.js). `date`: when the evidence was taken; product rules follow one product's build and must be re-checked when it changes. `family`: the rules that are one kind of evidence together (legend.families; the verdict counts them as one, verdict.json families). Rule definitions and collision notes taken from botscent 1.2.0 and BotD 2.0.0 (both MIT), and the conditions of fpscanner's checks (MIT), are credited in source_refs and THIRD_PARTY.md.

kinds.automation: A trace of an automation driver, or of the flags it launches the browser with: an automated browser.
kinds.spoofing: The browser misreports itself: stealth automation, or a privacy or user-agent tool.
kinds.product: Names one agent product. Tied to that product's build: dated, re-checked when the product changes.
kinds.cloud_host: The browser runs on a cloud machine without a GPU: a cloud browser that is not named.
kinds.extension: An extension or a debugger acted on this page inside the visitor's own browser.

halves.page: Read by cake.js in the visitor's page.
halves.collector: Read by cake's collect endpoint from cake.js's own requests.
halves.server: Read by the site's server on the page request (the server half's token).

strengths.hard: No known collision outside the software it points at: behaviour does not overturn it.
strengths.soft: Real evidence with a known collision (DevTools, privacy tools, uncommon browsers): weighed with behaviour.
strengths.weak: Goes into the reasons only; it changes no conclusion.

grades.measured: We measured it ourselves (lab recordings or tartini.ai).
grades.project-claim: The source project's own measurement, not reproduced by us.
grades.source: Read in a detector's source code or documentation, not measured.
grades.inferred: Inferred; neither measured nor taken from a detector.

families.phone_or_tablet: A computer passing as a phone or tablet. Each rule reads only a page whose user agent names an iPhone, iPad, iPod or Android device, so no desktop page is read. A developer's device emulation and user-agent switchers make all of them hold at once, so together they are one kind of evidence.

source_refs.rebrowser: rebrowser/rebrowser-bot-detector commit 55fa59b, README test descriptions; package.json says MIT but the repository has no LICENSE file, so only its published detection ideas are used, none of its code
source_refs.audit: AgentCake's signal audit of 2026-11-12 (119 signals, ids sig-NNN; ours)
source_refs.lab: AgentCake's lab recordings of 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-11 (ours: env.js, raw.js, bs.js and the lab server's request log)
source_refs.runs: AgentCake's own runs of agent products and of automation made to look human, on its test shop, 2026-11-13 and 2026-11-14 (ours; measured with agentcake eval), and of Playwright's phone and tablet emulation, 2026-11-19 (ours; cake.js uploads to its test collector, read with this rule table)
source_refs.platforms: AgentCake's simulation of the front doors websites put in front of it, 2026-11-18 (ours): the same visits uploaded with the headers CloudFront, an ALB, a Google Cloud load balancer, Cloudflare, nginx, Vercel and Caddy forward, after their documentation

source_refs.playwright: microsoft/playwright main at 09dab5d70932 (2026-11-19), Apache-2.0: packages/playwright-core/src/server/chromium/crPage.ts, calculateUserAgentMetadata and _updateUserAgent, which show what its phone emulation in Chromium sets (the user agent and its client hints) and leaves (navigator.platform, navigator.vendor); read, no code copied
source_refs.mdn: mdn/browser-compat-data at 589202441f49, CC0: api/NavigatorUAData.json (no version of Safari has navigator.userAgentData)

rules.title: The browser reports that it's controlled by automation software.
rules.detail: The navigator.webdriver property is true.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 22 of 22 Playwright sessions (12 headless, 10 headed); 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: 15 of 15 Playwright and Puppeteer visits with default settings; 0 of 3 human visits; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome.
rules.collisions: None among botscent's 44 human documents (a Windows VM, a Linux container, Safari, Firefox, an iPhone, DevTools open) or our 3 human visits. A person using a browser that automation launched would match. Stealth setups turn it off (see env.spoof.webdriver-getter-patched).

rules.title: The browser identifies itself as headless Chrome, a version of Chrome without a window that automation tools use.
rules.detail: The page's user agent or brand list includes HeadlessChrome.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions, 0 of 10 headed, 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: every headless visit that kept its user agent (V05-V07, V09-V12, V18); 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: No person browses headless; a person driving a remote headless session would match.

rules.title: The browser identifies itself as headless Chrome, a version of Chrome without a window that automation tools use.
rules.detail: The requests from cake.js include HeadlessChrome in their User-Agent or sec-ch-ua header.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: the collect requests of 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions; none of the headed or Claude in Chrome sessions.
rules.collisions: Same as env.auto.headless-ua: no person browses headless.

rules.title: The browser identifies itself as headless Chrome, a version of Chrome without a window that automation tools use.
rules.detail: The User-Agent or sec-ch-ua header of the page request includes HeadlessChrome.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: the page requests of 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions. tartini.ai 2026-11-10: 13 of 13 headless visits in botscent's server half; headed Playwright not matched.
rules.collisions: Same as env.auto.headless-ua.

rules.title: The requests don't include the language header that browsers usually send.
rules.detail: None of the requests from cake.js include an Accept-Language header. The requests have the same User-Agent as the page and include the browser's Sec-Fetch-Mode header. This is typical of chrome-headless-shell.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 1,324 of 1,324 collect requests from headless Playwright (chrome-headless-shell) had no Accept-Language; 1,273 of 1,273 from headed Playwright and Claude in Chrome had it. Lab 2026-11-09: 0 of 20 from chrome-headless-shell (V05) had it; 40 of 40 from the 3 human visits had it; new headless mode (V06, V07) sends it. Platform simulation 2026-11-18: chrome-headless-shell's own requests carry the page's User-Agent and Sec-Fetch-Mode, so the rule still holds for it; a person's requests through CloudFront's default settings arrive without Accept-Language too, which is why the last two conditions are there.
rules.collisions: None known when the requests arrive as the browser sent them: every browser a person uses sends Accept-Language. A front door that drops the header for every visitor (CloudFront's default settings, which also put "Amazon CloudFront" in the User-Agent; its UserAgentRefererHeaders origin request policy, which also drops the Sec-Fetch headers) fails the last two conditions and gives env.auto.collect-no-accept-language-proxy instead. A privacy tool that strips only Accept-Language would match (untested). Covers chrome-headless-shell (Playwright's and Puppeteer's default headless), not Chrome's new headless mode.

rules.title: The requests don't include the language header that browsers usually send. A proxy in front of AgentCake might have removed it.
rules.detail: The requests from cake.js have no Accept-Language header. The requests also have a different User-Agent from the page, or they don't include a Sec-Fetch-Mode header. Proxies and CDNs that rewrite requests, such as CloudFront with default settings, remove these headers for every visitor. In this case, AgentCake doesn't count the missing header as a sign of automation.
rules.evidence: Platform simulation 2026-11-18: a person's visit uploaded through CloudFront's default settings arrives without Accept-Language and with the User-Agent "Amazon CloudFront"; through CloudFront's UserAgentRefererHeaders origin request policy, with the browser's User-Agent but without Accept-Language and the Sec-Fetch headers. Before this rule split, both made the person an Agent.
rules.collisions: Every visitor whose requests pass such a front door matches, which is why it changes no conclusion. chrome-headless-shell behind it matches too and loses the hard rule; its page records (webdriver, the HeadlessChrome User-Agent) still give it away.

rules.title: The page shows signs of a debugging connection. Automation tools and open DevTools can cause this.
rules.detail: The browser serializes console arguments, which happens when a DevTools-protocol client has Runtime enabled.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 22 of 22 Playwright sessions; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: every Playwright and Puppeteer visit including the stealth (V08) and connect-over-CDP (V18) ones; 0 of 3 humans; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-16 (Chrome for Testing 1228; Playwright 1.64.1 as the protocol client): with a console recorder on the page (rrweb 2.0.0-alpha.18's console plugin, or a minimal one), the page's own console counted 3 formattings in 3 rounds with no protocol client at all; a frame of the probe's own counted 0, and 3 with Playwright, as the page's console did without a recorder. Since 2026-11-16 cake.js probes in such a frame (console frame) and only those counts are read; a record without console (an earlier cake.js) is read as before.
rules.collisions: Open DevTools trigger it too (rebrowser's README): a developer browsing with DevTools open matches. A site's own console recorder (rrweb's console plugin, analytics and error trackers) wraps the page's console and read like a protocol client on every visit to that site (tartini.ai 2026-11-16: the same counts on every session, the user's own included); cake.js has probed in a frame of its own since 2026-11-16, which no page script reaches, but a record without console (an earlier cake.js) may still carry such counts.

rules.title: Chrome is running with one of its browser protections turned off.
rules.detail: The page made 300 history.replaceState calls, and none of them was blocked. This happens when Chrome runs with --disable-ipc-flooding-protection.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 22 of 22 Playwright sessions applied 300; 4 of 4 Claude in Chrome stopped at 200. Lab 2026-11-09: every visit launched by Playwright or Puppeteer, the stealth one (V08) included; 0 of 3 humans; not V18, which connected to a Chrome it did not launch.
rules.collisions: A person who starts Chrome with --disable-ipc-flooding-protection (rare). Firefox and Safari throw instead of applying, so the rule is limited to Chrome user agents.

rules.title: An automation tool served this page directly, so the browser didn't load it from the network.
rules.detail: The automation tool served the page, and the browser didn't load it from the network.
rules.evidence: rebrowser documentInterception: an empty nextHopProtocol with bytes transferred never happens on a normal or cached load. No lab session intercepted its pages.
rules.collisions: None known (rebrowser). Pages served by a service worker report workerStart and are not matched.

rules.title: The page contains signs of Playwright, an automation tool.
rules.detail: The page has the __pwInitScripts and __playwright__binding__ global variables, which Playwright adds.
rules.evidence: rebrowser pwInitScripts. Playwright 1.64 left none in the lab (0 of 22 sessions), so this catches older or other Playwright builds only.
rules.collisions: None known; a page's own variable named like playwright... would match.

rules.title: The page contains signs of Puppeteer, an automation tool.
rules.detail: The page has the puppeteer_* and __puppeteer* global variables, which Puppeteer adds.
rules.evidence: rebrowser exposeFunctionLeak and sourceUrlLeak. None in the lab: Puppeteer 24 (V09) left no global.
rules.collisions: None known; a page's own variable named puppeteer_... would match.

rules.title: An automation tool added its own function to the page.
rules.detail: The automation driver added a function to the page and marked it __installed.
rules.evidence: rebrowser exposeFunctionLeak: page.exposeFunction leaves a readable wrapper. None in the lab (the lab scripts exposed no function).
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: The page contains signs of Selenium or ChromeDriver automation.
rules.detail: The page has variables that Selenium or ChromeDriver adds: cdc_, $wdc_, __webdriver_*, and __selenium_*.
rules.evidence: BotD distinctive properties and document attributes, the cdc_ pattern from rebrowser. None in the lab (no Selenium run).
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: The page contains signs of older automation tools or of tools that show websites inside apps. Some of your site's own scripts can also add these signs.
rules.detail: The page has global variables left by older automation or embedding tools, such as PhantomJS, Nightmare, CEF, Awesomium, or WebdriverIO.
rules.evidence: BotD's list of distinctive properties. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Some of the names are generic (emit for CoachJS, spawn for Rhino, geb), so a site's own script can define them; CEF and CefSharp also show web pages to people inside desktop apps.

rules.title: An automation tool might have added functions to the page.
rules.detail: The window object has unnamed native functions. Tools that use CDP Runtime.addBinding add functions like these.
rules.evidence: rebrowser cdpBindingGlobals (rated yellow there). None in the lab.
rules.collisions: A page's own scripts can create functions that look the same (rebrowser).

rules.title: The browser identifies itself as Chrome but is missing a standard Chrome feature.
rules.detail: The browser identifies itself as Chrome but doesn't have the window.chrome object that Chrome provides. Headless builds such as chrome-headless-shell behave the same way.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions (chrome-headless-shell); 0 of 10 headed; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: V05 (headless shell); 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: Embedded Chromium in apps (Android WebView is excluded by its wv token, Electron by its token; other embedders untested).

rules.title: The browser gives conflicting answers about notification permissions.
rules.detail: The Notification.permission property is denied, but the permission state from permissions.query is prompt. This is typical of chrome-headless-shell.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions; 0 of 10 headed; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: V05 (headless shell); 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: None known: only chrome-headless-shell answers this way (rebrowser, BotD).

rules.title: This desktop Chrome browser reports no plugins.
rules.detail: The navigator.plugins list is empty on desktop Chrome.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions; 0 of 10 headed; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: V05; 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: Chrome with its PDF viewer turned off ("Download PDFs") also reports no plugins.

rules.title: The browser draws graphics in software, which can mean that Chrome is running without a window.
rules.detail: WebGL uses SwiftShader on a desktop that isn't running Linux. On those systems, Chrome 138+ uses SwiftShader only in headless mode or when a special flag is set.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 12 of 12 headless Playwright sessions on macOS; 0 of 10 headed; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: V05; 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: Chrome started with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, or a machine whose GPU Chrome blocks (rebrowser: no automatic fallback since Chrome 138). Linux is left to env.cloud.linux-swiftshader.

rules.title: The browser reports the same brand information as Chrome for Testing, which automation tools use by default.
rules.detail: On a desktop, the brand list has only Chromium. Chrome for Testing, the default browser for Playwright and Puppeteer, reports this brand list.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 10 of 10 headed Playwright sessions (Chrome for Testing); headless ones carry HeadlessChrome instead; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. Lab 2026-11-09: V06; 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: People who browse with a plain Chromium build (Linux distribution packages, ungoogled-chromium). Edge, Brave and Opera add their own brand and do not match.

rules.title: The page area is exactly the default size of an automation tool.
rules.detail: The viewport is exactly Playwright's default of 1280x720 or Puppeteer's default of 800x600.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-09: every visit Playwright launched (1280x720) and every Puppeteer visit (800x600); not V18, which attached to a Chrome it did not launch; 0 of 3 humans. The 2026-11-11 lab set its own 1280x800 viewport, so it does not match there.
rules.collisions: An ordinary window can end up at these sizes (rebrowser rates it a hint, not proof).

rules.title: An automation script called browser functions on this page.
rules.detail: The stack trace of a DOM call includes pptr:, UtilityScript, or __puppeteer_evaluation_script__.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-09: Playwright's page.evaluate clicks (V12) left UtilityScript in the stack of the hooked querySelector. Off by default: cake.js must wrap the site's own DOM methods to see it.
rules.collisions: None known. Wrapping the site's document.querySelector and friends can break a site or slow it down, so the site owner turns it on in settings.

rules.title: The page is open inside a desktop app's built-in browser.
rules.detail: The page runs inside an Electron app's built-in browser.
rules.evidence: BotD detectProcess, detectUserAgent and detectAppVersion. Desktop AI apps with their own browser are named by the name layer's user-agent list; this only says an app's browser was used.
rules.collisions: People read web pages inside many desktop apps built on Electron.

rules.title: The visitor uses an old browser engine that's associated with automation.
rules.detail: PhantomJS or SlimerJS was detected through the user agent, the error stack, or a missing Function.prototype.bind.
rules.evidence: BotD detectUserAgent, detectErrorTrace and detectFunctionBind. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: None known: nobody browses with these engines.

rules.title: The visitor uses Sequentum, the browser of a scraping tool.
rules.detail: The window.external object includes Sequentum.
rules.evidence: BotD detectWindowExternal. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: The browser draws graphics with the same software that older automated browsers used.
rules.detail: WebGL reports the renderer Mesa OffScreen from the vendor Brian Paul. Old versions of headless Chrome reported the same values.
rules.evidence: BotD detectWebGL. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: The page has focus, but its browser window reports no size.
rules.detail: The focused page's window has an outer size of 0x0.
rules.evidence: BotD detectWindowSize. In the lab only unfocused pages had a 0x0 window (a tab opened in the background), which BotD and this rule leave alone.
rules.collisions: BotD skips unfocused pages because a background tab has a 0x0 window; other collisions untested.

rules.title: The browser doesn't report any languages.
rules.detail: The navigator.languages list is empty.
rules.evidence: BotD detectLanguagesLengthInconsistency (older headless Chrome). None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Untested; privacy settings that empty the list would match.

rules.title: The browser's automation flag was changed. Automation tools can do this to hide that they control the browser.
rules.detail: Browsers use the navigator.webdriver property to report automation. In this browser, the property isn't the built-in one: its getter was replaced, navigator has a separate copy, or the property was removed.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-09: the stealth Playwright visit (V08: webdriver false through a non-native getter) 2 of 2; 0 of 3 humans; 0 of 4 Claude in Chrome. None in the 2026-11-11 lab.
rules.collisions: Anti-fingerprinting extensions that wrap navigator getters (untested).

rules.title: A browser function doesn't match the browser's reported identity.
rules.detail: The length of eval's source code doesn't match the browser engine that the page reports.
rules.evidence: BotD detectEvalLengthInconsistency: a user agent claiming another engine. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: User-agent switcher extensions.

rules.title: The browser's list of file types has an unexpected structure.
rules.detail: The navigator.mimeTypes list has a structure that this browser doesn't normally produce.
rules.evidence: BotD detectMimeTypesConsistent. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Fingerprint-spoofing extensions.

rules.title: The browser reports conflicting identity details.
rules.detail: The navigator.productSub value doesn't match the browser that the page reports.
rules.evidence: BotD detectProductSub. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: User-agent switcher extensions.

rules.title: The browser's plugin list has an unexpected structure.
rules.detail: The navigator.plugins list isn't a genuine PluginArray object.
rules.evidence: BotD detectPluginsArray (a stealth script's replacement list). None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Fingerprint-spoofing extensions.

rules.title: The page and a background script report different browser details.
rules.detail: A web worker reports a different user agent, platform, or brand list than the page.
rules.evidence: rebrowser workerConsistency: values faked by page scripts do not reach workers. No difference in the 2026-11-11 lab. fpscanner hasMismatchPlatformWorker: iOS in desktop mode (the default on iPad, an option on iPhone) reports MacIntel in the page and the device in a worker, so a platform that differs only that way, on a page with a touch screen, is not counted (2026-11-19). Each of the three tests counts as not holding when its input was not recorded, so the rule reads every other session as before.
rules.collisions: User-agent switcher extensions that patch only the page. Differences in languages or CPU count are left out because privacy extensions cause them (rebrowser). An iPad or iPhone showing the desktop site reports MacIntel in the page and iPad or iPhone in a worker: not counted when the page reports more than one touch point, which no Mac does.

rules.title: Built-in browser functions were changed. Privacy extensions can also change these functions.
rules.detail: Native browser functions were replaced or wrapped.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-09: the stealth visit (V08) 2 of 2; 0 of 3 humans. None in the 2026-11-11 lab.
rules.collisions: Fingerprint-spoofing and privacy extensions wrap the same functions (rebrowser).

rules.title: The browser reports conflicting operating system details.
rules.detail: The operating system in the user agent doesn't match navigator.platform.
rules.evidence: rebrowser platformMismatch: overriding the user agent leaves navigator.platform and the client hints telling the truth. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: User-agent switcher extensions.

rules.title: The browser appears to run on a Mac but reports another operating system.
rules.detail: The user agent and navigator.platform report Windows, Linux, or Android. However, the browser resolves the -apple-system or BlinkMacSystemFont font name. Apple's systems resolve these names, and other systems do only when they add aliases for them, for example with fontconfig on Linux.
rules.evidence: Our test page on this Mac, 2026-11-14: Camoufox claiming Linux or Windows resolves -apple-system (3 of 3), fingerprint-suite (Chromium with a generated Windows or Linux fingerprint) resolves BlinkMacSystemFont (4 of 4); the same Mac's Chrome and Camoufox claiming macOS agree. Both tools bring the claimed system's fonts, voices and graphics limits, so only these names give the Mac away. Engines map them only on Apple's systems, unless the system gives the name an alias (fontconfig can on Linux). Not yet measured on real visitors.
rules.collisions: On a Mac, a user-agent switcher that also changes navigator.platform, and a developer tool's device emulation (a phone's user agent on a Mac). On Linux, a fontconfig alias for -apple-system or BlinkMacSystemFont, which some developers set so that font stacks starting with Apple's names look right.

rules.title: Requests from this visit report different operating systems.
rules.detail: In this visit, the User-Agent header of cake.js's requests changes between operating systems, such as macOS and Windows. Browsers send the same operating system in every request, but automation tools that change it can leave some requests unchanged.
rules.evidence: Our runs of 2026-11-14: every session of fingerprint-suite (20; Playwright with generated Windows or Linux fingerprints) and of Puppeteer's page.setUserAgent (10). The batches cake.js sends with sendBeacon as a page is left carry the browser's own User-Agent (macOS), the other requests the changed one. None of the other 151 automated sessions (Camoufox changes the User-Agent inside the browser, for every request) and none of the recorder's 11 people.
rules.collisions: An extension or proxy that rewrites the User-Agent of only some requests. Versions are not compared (a browser updated across a restart), and switching a phone or tablet to the desktop site stays within one family (iPhone, iPad and Mac; Android, Linux and ChromeOS), so neither counts.

rules.title: This desktop Chrome browser doesn't report its brand information.
rules.detail: The brand list is empty on desktop Chrome. Puppeteer's setUserAgent can cause this.
rules.evidence: rebrowser platformMismatch: never happens in a real desktop Chrome. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Apps that set a custom WebView user agent on mobile (excluded).

rules.title: The user agent identifies a phone or tablet, but the browser reports a computer's operating system.
rules.detail: The user agent identifies an iPhone, iPad, iPod, or Android device. However, navigator.platform reports a computer's operating system, such as Windows or macOS. Phone emulation in desktop browsers can leave navigator.platform unchanged.
rules.evidence: fpscanner hasPlatformMismatch flags a user agent that names Apple's systems with a Windows or Linux navigator.platform, and one that names Linux, as Android's do, with a Mac or Windows platform. Here only user agents that name a phone or tablet are read (desktop ones stay with env.spoof.ua-platform-mismatch), and for an iPhone, iPad or iPod only a computer's Linux counts, since an Android phone given an iPhone's user agent reports ARM Linux. Playwright's phone emulation in Chromium (crPage.ts) overrides the user agent and its client hints but never navigator.platform, which keeps the computer's. Android with Linux x86_64 is left out: Android's emulator and Android on x86 report it. Our runs of 2026-11-19 (Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 149, on a Mac): its Pixel 7 and Galaxy S9+ emulation 2 of 2 (navigator.platform MacIntel); its iPhone 15 and iPad Pro 11 emulation on a Mac report MacIntel, which this rule leaves to env.spoof.ios-ua-chromium-engine; desktop Chromium 0. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: A developer's device emulation in a desktop browser (Chrome DevTools, Playwright) and user-agent switchers that set a phone's user agent and keep navigator.platform. Real iPhones, iPads and iPods report iPhone, iPad or iPod; Android devices report an ARM Linux (Linux armv8l, armv81, aarch64).

rules.title: The user agent identifies an iPhone, iPad, or iPod, but the browser has features of Chrome's engine.
rules.detail: Common browsers on iPhone and iPad use Apple's WebKit engine. WebKit reports Apple as navigator.vendor and doesn't have navigator.userAgentData. This browser matches Chrome in at least one of them.
rules.evidence: Playwright's iPhone and iPad emulation in Chromium (crPage.ts) sets the user agent and its client hints, with iOS as their platform; Chromium keeps navigator.userAgentData and reports Google Inc. as navigator.vendor. Browsers on iPhone and iPad run on WebKit, which has no navigator.userAgentData (MDN browser-compat-data) and reports Apple Computer, Inc. as its vendor. Our runs of 2026-11-19 (Playwright 1.64.1, Chromium 149, on a Mac): its iPhone 15 and iPad Pro 11 emulation 2 of 2 (navigator.userAgentData with iOS as its platform, Google Inc.); its iPhone 15 emulation in WebKit 0 (WebKit itself); desktop Chromium 0. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: Browsers that bring their own engine to iPhone and iPad, which the EU allows since iOS 17.4 (none seen). A developer's iPhone emulation in Chrome DevTools, and user-agent switchers that set an iPhone's user agent in Chrome.

rules.title: The user agent identifies an Android device, but the browser reports an Apple GPU.
rules.detail: WebGL reports an Apple GPU. Android devices use GPUs from other manufacturers, such as Qualcomm and Arm. On a Mac with Apple silicon, Chrome reports an Apple GPU, even when it emulates an Android phone.
rules.evidence: fpscanner hasGPUMismatch (its WebGL part; cake.js reads no WebGPU) flags an Apple GPU with a user agent that does not name Apple's systems; here only user agents that name Android are read. Chromium emulating an Android phone on a Mac keeps the Mac's WebGL renderer (ANGLE with an Apple M-series GPU). None in the lab.
rules.collisions: A developer's Android emulation in Chrome DevTools on a Mac; Android's emulator on a Mac may name the Mac's GPU in its renderer (untested). Android devices report Adreno, Mali, PowerVR, Xclipse or similar GPUs.

rules.title: The page is open in Cursor's in-app browser.
rules.detail: The user agent includes Cursor/<version>.
rules.evidence: botscent: Cursor 3.23.12 on macOS, 2 of 2 documents named cursor-browser; Safari on the same Mac human.
rules.collisions: A person browsing Cursor's in-app browser by hand is named cursor-browser by design: it names the browser, not who acts in it. Anyone can send the token.

rules.title: The browser identifies itself as Cloudflare Browser Run, a hosted browser.
rules.detail: The page's navigator reports the user agent Kitesurf/ or the platform Cloudflare Workers.
rules.evidence: botscent registry/page.json, replayed on every benchmark sheet with 57 human control documents.
rules.collisions: No person's browser declares the hosted engine. Forgeable like any declaration.

rules.title: The browser matches Muse's cloud browser.
rules.detail: The page has 1Password's credential accessors. The browser runs on Linux x86_64 with Chrome 139+ and SwiftShader.
rules.evidence: tartini.ai 2026-11-11: botscent's page half named muse in 4 of 4 Muse visits (confirmed by the user). botscent 2026-10-03: Muse 21 of 21 documents, 0 of 82 human documents, 0 of 4 with 1Password.
rules.collisions: A person matches only with 1Password, Linux and Chrome launched with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader (untested; rare): unless the timeline shows the agent acting and a hand-off, that session is Muse's (Agent). Another automation host running 1Password would be named muse.

rules.title: The browser matches Grok Bot's cloud computer.
rules.detail: The browser runs Chrome 139+ on Linux x86_64 and renders WebGL in software with SwiftShader. It also matches 5 of the 6 machine details of Grok Bot's cloud computer.
rules.evidence: botscent: Grok Bot 67 of 67 documents with all six signs (28 September to 3 October), 0 of 90 human documents, 0 of 210 other agents' documents. Not measured by us yet.
rules.collisions: A person working inside Grok Bot's own computer is named grok-bot by design; unless the timeline shows Grok Bot acting and a hand-off, the session is Grok Bot's (Agent). A stock Ubuntu cloud desktop holds 3 of the 6 signs and no SwiftShader. Another product on the same machine image would be named grok-bot.

rules.title: The browser matches Instinct's cloud desktop.
rules.detail: The page's credential methods are wrapped, and GeeTest's accessor pair is present.
rules.evidence: botscent: replayed on every benchmark sheet with 57 human control documents; each half counts only with the other.
rules.collisions: Untested: a credential or CAPTCHA extension that wraps the same methods, or a person on the same remote desktop.

rules.title: The page is open in the Codex in-app browser.
rules.detail: The Codex in-app browser has 3 known signs: its prompt shape, an empty keyboard layout, and an overlay. This page shows 2 of them.
rules.evidence: botscent: a person in the Codex in-app browser matches too (4 of 4 documents); replayed on every benchmark sheet with 57 human control documents.
rules.collisions: A person browsing the Codex in-app browser by hand is named codex-browser by design: it names the browser, not who acts in it.

rules.title: ChatGPT for Chrome was active on this page.
rules.detail: The ChatGPT for Chrome activity badge was on the page's favicon.
rules.evidence: botscent: 71 samples in 17 documents were a badged icon link. Not measured by us.
rules.collisions: A person who takes the tab over in the seconds before the badge is removed.

rules.title: Claude in Chrome was active on this page.
rules.detail: The page has the claude-agent-glow-border ID and related IDs, which Claude in Chrome adds as its activity marker.
rules.evidence: botscent's older measurements. Lab 2026-11-11: Claude in Chrome 1.0.106 hides its marker in a closed shadow root, so 0 of 4 sessions matched; env.ext.closed-shadow-host sees that version.
rules.collisions: A person taking the tab over before the marker is removed.

rules.title: Claude in Chrome's working indicator appeared on this page.
rules.detail: The indicator was shown on the page.
rules.evidence: agentcake/data/agent_markers.json: Claude in Chrome 1.0.107 draws its 'Claude is working here' tag inside a closed shadow root while its agent works and takes it away when it stops (its agent-visual-indicator.js, read 2026-11-13); cake.js hit-tests where the tag is drawn (claude-chrome.working) and the recorder checks the same spots and one more (claude-chrome.recorder); versions before 1.0.105 put ids in the page itself (claude-chrome.page-dom). Lab 2026-11-11 (1.0.106): the closed-shadow host on 13 of 13 pages. Not yet seen in a recording of 1.0.107: re-grade after the hand-off recordings.
rules.collisions: Another extension that draws a clickable mark at the same spots from an attribute-less display: contents host (none known; untested). The recorder's check also counts the tab pill, which shows while the tab is shared with Claude and the agent is idle.

rules.title: The browser shows signs of running on a cloud machine.
rules.detail: The browser reports that it's Chrome 139+ on Linux x86_64. It uses SwiftShader, a software renderer, to draw WebGL graphics.
rules.evidence: botscent's cloud-host clauses (isCloudHost, isSoftwareRenderer), shared by Muse and Grok Bot: Chrome 139+ no longer falls back to SwiftShader without a flag. Not measured on our own cloud runs yet.
rules.collisions: A person on Linux whose Chrome runs with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader, or headless Chrome on a Linux CI machine (an automated browser anyway).

rules.title: The browser draws graphics in software, as on cloud servers and virtual machines.
rules.detail: WebGL uses Mesa's llvmpipe software renderer on Linux. This can happen on machines without a GPU.
rules.evidence: Software rendering is a cloud-machine sign (our signal audit lists llvmpipe); no measurement.
rules.collisions: People on Linux virtual machines or remote desktops without a GPU.

rules.title: The requests that cake.js sent came from a cloud or content delivery network.
rules.detail: The requests from cake.js came from a cloud or CDN network.
rules.evidence: tartini.ai 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-11: Muse came from Cloudflare's network both times. Needs cake on a server (its network facts); local mode only sees 127.0.0.1.
rules.collisions: VPN and Cloudflare WARP users, and people browsing from a company cloud desktop. A datacenter IP never makes a Bot on its own.

rules.title: A browser extension added an element to the page.
rules.detail: An element with a closed shadow root was added under <body>. It's a <div> with no attributes and display: contents.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: Claude in Chrome 1.0.106 added it to 13 of 13 pages the DOM watch covered (4 of 4 sessions); 0 of the Playwright pages; a script-added plain <div> (display block, motest-01) does not match.
rules.collisions: Other extensions that draw into a closed shadow root the same way are untested (no human control with other extensions yet). It says an extension drew on this page, not that it was acting at a given moment.

rules.title: The visible page area became shorter. Chrome's debugging bar can cause this.
rules.detail: The viewport became 40-72 pixels shorter with the same width. Chrome's "started debugging this browser" bar takes up this space when it appears.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: cic-01's open tab went from 958 to 902 px (56 px) when the debugger attached for the next run. Lab 2026-11-09: the user's own tab shrank the same way while Claude in Chrome ran in another tab.
rules.collisions: The bar belongs to the whole browser: a person's own tab in that browser shrinks too. A toolbar of similar height appearing would match. On a phone or tablet, the browser's address bar hides and shows as the page scrolls and changes the viewport height the same way, so the rule isn't read when the browser says it is a phone or tablet.

rules.title: The first page was opened from another site without a click, tap, or key press.
rules.detail: The Sec-Fetch-Site header is cross-site, and there's no Sec-Fetch-User header.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 4 of 4 Claude in Chrome first pages; Playwright opened its pages as none with ?1. Lab 2026-11-09: 4 of 4 Claude in Chrome; 0 of 3 humans (typed address: none with ?1).
rules.collisions: A person sent on by another site's script without a click (link shorteners and redirect pages such as t.co, some sign-in flows).

rules.title: The first page loaded in the background, which can happen when an extension opens a tab.
rules.detail: When the page loaded, it was hidden and didn't have focus. The page's window also reports no outer size.
rules.evidence: Lab 2026-11-11: 4 of 4 Claude in Chrome first pages. Lab 2026-11-09: 2 of 4; 0 of 3 humans.
rules.collisions: A person who opens a link in a background tab (untested).

rules.title: A debugging tool sent input to the hidden page.
rules.detail: While the page was hidden in the background, it received a trusted pointerdown event. A pointer press creates this event.
rules.evidence: botscent: no person can click in a hidden document; none in 44 human documents. Lab 2026-11-11: Claude in Chrome brought each tab to the front before acting, so none matched.
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: The hidden page received input while reporting that it had focus.
rules.detail: The page received trusted input while it was hidden. At the same time, it reported that it had focus. This indicates focus emulation.
rules.evidence: botscent: focus while hidden needs Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled; none in 44 human documents. None in the lab.
rules.collisions: None known.

rules.title: An agent extension is installed in this browser.
rules.detail: The browser loads public files from an agent extension through web_accessible_resources.
rules.evidence: From our signal audit. Off by default: probing which extensions a visitor has installed is a device fingerprint (visitors in Europe must consent first), and installed is not in use. The list of extensions to probe is not defined yet.
rules.collisions: Says the extension is installed, not that it acted: a person with the extension installed matches on every page.
